name: Passive Neighbors Force a Punctured Cube Fiber
statement: Let $K\subsetneq A$ be ample, let $D=A\setminus K$ have one passive restriction, and let $L$ be the corresponding active lower slice. For $d\in D$, let $Z(d)=\{z:d^{\oplus z}\in K\}$ and $t(d)=|Z(d)|$. Then $d^{\oplus T}\in K$ for every nonempty $T\subseteq Z(d)$, and $|K|\ge |L|+\sum_{d\in D}(2^{t(d)}-1)$. If $L$ is nonempty and $Z_0=\{z:S_z\ne\varnothing\}$, then every $z\in Z_0$ contributes an additional collar vertex and $|K|\ge |L|+|Z_0|+\sum_{d\in D}(2^{t(d)}-1)$.
proof: Condition $K$ on the active word of $d$ and all passive coordinates outside $Z(d)$. The resulting ample family contains every singleton of $Q_{Z(d)}$ but not the empty word. Its ample complement contains the empty word; isometry prevents it from containing any other word because a geodesic would begin with a forbidden singleton. Hence the conditioned family is the punctured cube. Fibers belonging to distinct $d$ have distinct active restrictions, giving the first count. When $L$ is nonempty, the ample two-section class in every nonempty passive direction is connected, so its sections $L$ and $M_z$ intersect. Choosing one intersection point per direction gives pairwise distinct collar vertices outside the punctured fibers and proves the strengthened count.
